title: Collab user count doesn't decrement when a user leaves (stuck at high-water-mark)
description:
USER REPORT: after users LEAVE a collab session, the participant count keeps showing the MAX it reached; it never decrements on leave.

Observed sequence (user):
- A joins -> 'waiting for others'
- B joins -> '2 users'
- B LEAVES -> still '2 users'   (should drop to 1 / 'waiting')
- C joins -> '3 users'          (should be 2 = A+C)
- C LEAVES -> still '3 users'   (should drop to 1)
So the count tracks a high-water-mark / stale connections and never shrinks on disconnect.

ROOT CAUSE (file:line): packages/authoring-ui/src/collab/CollabControls.tsx:38-64 useCollabStatus(). The status-pill count (status.peers) is derived from y-webrtc's CONNECTION-level 'peers' event: onPeers (lines 51-55) does setPeers(Math.max(webrtcPeers.length, bcPeers.length)). y-webrtc's webrtcPeers/bcPeers come from room.webrtcConns / room.bcConns (node_modules .../y-webrtc/src/y-webrtc.js: a connection is removed ONLY on a clean WebRTC 'close', lines 211-222). Crucially the connection layer has NO timeout/TTL: on an UNCLEAN leave (tab close, network drop, crash, or any case where the WebRTC 'close' / signaling teardown does not fire) the connection lingers in webrtcConns/bcConns forever and no 'peers' event with the shrunk array is emitted, so the pill never decrements -- while every subsequent join still fires an 'added' event and the count climbs. That is the exact monotonic/high-water-mark signature the user sees.

Architectural divergence (the real defect): there are TWO independent count sources.
 1. STATUS PILL count = useCollabStatus -> y-webrtc connection 'peers' event. NO TTL, only decrements on a clean 'close'. <- this is the stuck one.
 2. AVATARS / usePeers = awarenessController.getPeers() over awareness.getStates() (awareness.ts readPeers, CollabContext usePeers). This path HAS removal: y-protocols awareness fires 'change' with removed[] on the built-in 30s outdatedTimeout, and detach() calls awareness.setLocalState(null) for an instant clean-leave removal (awareness.ts:184-186). reconnect.ts documents the 30s reap. So avatars self-heal; the pill does not. The two sources can (and do) disagree.

REPRODUCED (scratch vitest, since removed):
 - readPeers() over a real loopback Awareness mesh: add B -> 1 peer; removeAwarenessStates(B) -> 0. Awareness path decrements correctly.
 - The useCollabStatus onPeers reducer replayed with the y-webrtc event shape: clean events (arrays that shrink) DO decrement (0,1,0,1,0). But the STALE-CONNECTION case -- B joins (count 1), B's tab closes with NO clean close (no 'peers' event), then C joins -> event carries webrtcPeers:[B,C] -> count shows 2 even though only A+C are present. This matches the user's stuck-at-max sequence: the leaver's connection is never pruned, joins keep adding.

SCOPE / BREADTH:
 - Status-pill label CollabControls.tsx:193-195 -> affected (sticks at max).
 - peerCountAdvice >15 warning threshold: CollabControls.tsx:191 AND ShareDialog.tsx:188 both feed status.peers into peerCountAdvice. A stale-inflated count can FALSELY trip the >15 'large group / split into rooms' warning. Affected.
 - Avatars/remote cursors (CollabPresence.tsx, PresenceAvatars.tsx) read usePeers() (awareness) -> NOT the same bug; they prune on clean leave instantly and within ~30s otherwise. But on an unclean drop a departed peer's avatar/cursor CAN linger up to ~30s, and the pill/avatar counts can disagree -- a UX inconsistency in its own right.

FIX DIRECTION:
 - Derive the participant count from the CURRENT awareness states (the same source the avatars use: awarenessController.getPeers().length / awareness.getStates() minus self), NOT from y-webrtc's connection 'peers' event. That gives a single source of truth, decrements on clean leave (setLocalState(null)), and self-prunes stale entries via the 30s outdatedTimeout. Concretely: have useCollabStatus subscribe to the awarenessController (onPeersChange) and count peers from awareness, or replace status.peers with usePeers().length.
 - Do NOT track a max/monotonic counter or an add-only Set. The connection 'peers' event is fine for signaling/connectivity health (reconnect.ts) but must not be the participant-count authority because it has no TTL.
 - After the fix, the user's A/B+/B-/C+/C- sequence should read 1/2/1/2/1 (participants incl. local), and the pill + avatars should agree.

Acceptance: a unit test driving awareness add+remove (and the user's leave sequence) asserting the count DECREMENTS; ideally an e2e/multipeer test where a peer detaches and the survivors' count drops. Presence/awareness is testable in-process (no Playwright needed).
